evals.prompt: Tutor me on the Workspace initiative. Sources: the RFC draft PR https://ghe.example.com/acme/workspace-rfcs/pull/77, the workspace PR https://ghe.example.com/acme/workspace-app/pull/7, all tabs of https://docs.google.com/document/d/example-workspace-design/edit, the Jira initiative https://jira.example.com/browse/PROJ-123, and my local repos in ~/apps. Build a knowledge base and start tutoring.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full pipeline: gathers all six source kinds via the right tools (GitHub MCP for both PRs incl. changed-file content, Drive MCP list_document_tabs + per-tab read for ALL tabs, Jira MCP jira_search_issues for PROJ-123 plus its children, local ~/apps repos matched to the topic), stages them with stage-learn-sources into one manifest, runs /tutor-setup to build a grounded StudyVault, then starts /tutor with a diagnostic session.
expectations: Uses GitHub MCP get_pull_request/get_pull_request_files (or gh CLI for enterprise hosts) to pull BOTH PRs, including the RFC PR's changed-file content (the RFC markdown), not just metadata
Fetches ALL tabs of the Google Doc via list_document_tabs then read_document/export per tab — never only the currently-open tab
Fetches the Jira initiative PROJ-123 via jira_search_issues with issueKeys, and pulls child epics/stories via parentKeys
Passes the enterprise ghe.example.com repos as full git URLs (or via GitHub MCP), not as owner/repo shorthand that resolves to public github.com
Scans ~/apps, shortlists repos matching the topic, confirms with the user, and stages them with --local

Stages everything via stage-learn-sources into one manifest, runs /tutor-setup for the StudyVault, presents a concise learning brief, then starts /tutor with a diagnostic whose questions test understanding (not trivia) and randomize the correct option's position

evals.prompt: Teach me this project.
evals.expected_output: Detects that the current directory is a repo, treats it as the primary source, asks only for missing inputs (extra sources, focus, depth), stages it, runs /tutor-setup in codebase mode, then /tutor.
expectations: Infers the current directory as a local repo source instead of asking for a path it can determine
Asks only for what is still unknown (additional sources, focus areas, depth) in one concise batch
Stages the repo and runs /tutor-setup in codebase mode, then starts /tutor
Does not invent private repo names, Google Doc IDs, or Jira keys

evals.prompt: I already ran the prep earlier in ./.learn-project — just quiz me now.
evals.expected_output: Detects the existing stage from the staging root and resumes: if a StudyVault exists it goes straight to /tutor; if only a manifest exists it runs /tutor-setup first; it does not restart gathering from scratch.
expectations: Inspects the staging root to detect the current stage before doing anything
Resumes at the correct phase (straight to /tutor when a StudyVault exists) instead of re-gathering sources
Tells the user the detected stage and what it will do next before acting
Only re-runs /tutor-setup if the sources changed or the vault is missing

evals.prompt: Onboard me on our billing service using the design doc at https://docs.google.com/document/d/ABC123/edit and the Jira epic BILL-42.
evals.expected_output: Document/context-only run: exports all tabs of the Google Doc, pulls the Jira epic and its child issues, stages them (no repo), runs /tutor-setup in document mode, then /tutor.
expectations: Exports ALL tabs of the Google Doc, not just one, and stages it as a doc
Pulls Jira epic BILL-42 and its children via parentKeys and stages the summary as context
Selects document mode (no code repo present) and runs /tutor-setup then /tutor
Grounds notes in staged sources — every claim cites a staged path or doc/tab section (cite-or-refuse)

evals.prompt: tutor-setup isn't installed. Just teach me this repo anyway.
evals.expected_output: Ensures prerequisites first: installs tutor-setup and tutor via agentbrew's native path (bevibing/tutor-skills), and only if install fails tells the user exactly what to run instead of faking a vault.
expectations: Checks for tutor-setup/tutor and installs both via agentbrew install --from bevibing/tutor-skills before proceeding
Falls back to npx skills add only if agentbrew is unavailable
Refuses to fabricate a StudyVault if installation fails and tells the user the exact command to run
Proceeds with the normal pipeline once the upstream skills are available

evals.prompt: The Google Doc export hit an SSO login page and one repo is private. Learn what you can from the rest.
evals.expected_output: Treats blocked sources gracefully: backgrounds/polls the SSO source rather than idling, skips the unfetchable ones, stages the reachable sources, and lists the blocked items in the summary — without reconfiguring any MCP.
expectations: Does not idle on the SSO page — stages reachable sources first and reports the blocked one to poll/resume
Skips unfetchable private sources and continues with what is available
Never reconfigures or 'repairs' an MCP server on failure
Lists the missing/blocked sources explicitly in the final summary

evals.prompt: Quiz me on this project. But make the questions actually test whether I understand it — the last tutor asked me to memorize requirement IDs and one question was unclear.
evals.expected_output: A diagnostic whose questions test meaning and application (why/how/consequences/scenarios), are each self-contained and unambiguous, avoid recall of labels/list-names/spec IDs, and stay answerable from the grounded vault; when the user flags a question as bad, it is discarded and regenerated as a meaning-based question.
expectations: Questions test understanding — why/how/consequences or applying a concept to a scenario — not recall of terminology, list names, or requirement/spec IDs
Each question is self-contained and unambiguous, defining any term it depends on instead of using underspecified phrasing
Questions are phrased in clean, natural, grammatical English — awkward or broken wording is fixed before presenting
The diagnostic is ordered major-first: big-picture, highest-importance concepts before supporting details and edge cases
The correct option is randomly positioned across questions — no positional pattern (e.g. never always the first option)
Every question offers an explicit 'I don't know — teach me' option; picking it triggers a concise grounded explanation and marks the concept for review rather than scoring a wrong guess
A concise, refined learning brief is presented before the quiz starts (teach before testing), not a quiz cold-start
Every question's correct answer traces to a staged source (cite-or-refuse); a question the vault cannot answer is treated as bad, not hard
When the user flags a question as bad (trivia, unclear, or badly worded), the tutor discards it and regenerates a meaning-based, cleanly-worded version, preferring application/analysis over recall

evals.prompt: Keep quizzing me, but track what I know per section as a percentage and only ask about things I don't know yet — big-picture first, then details.
evals.expected_output: Maintains live mastery state in the vault: a known % per section (mastered concepts / total), recomputed after each answer, and selects each next question from the lowest-known section starting with big-picture concepts before details, never re-asking already-mastered concepts while unknown ones remain.
expectations: Records a mastery % per section in the Learning Dashboard as coverage (mastered concepts / total concepts), not just accuracy on tested questions
Reads the tracker before each question and updates it after each answer so it always knows which concepts remain unanswered
Selects the next question from the section with the lowest known %, and within it the most fundamental big-picture concept still not-known before any detail or edge case
Does not re-ask concepts already mastered while not-known concepts remain, except in explicit hard-mode reinforcement
After each round reports the updated per-section % and the remaining concepts, and treats a section as done only at 100% known

evals.prompt: Before you quiz me, verify every question is actually answerable from the vault — last time one question had no grounded answer.
evals.expected_output: Runs the verification gate after tutor-setup and before /tutor: re-answers each question from vault notes only, discards/regenerates any the vault cannot support, verifies note claims against cited staged spans, and reports the pass/discard/flag counts before starting the quiz.
expectations: Runs a pre-quiz verification pass after the vault exists and before /tutor starts
Attempts to answer each question using only vault notes (not staged sources directly or general knowledge)
Discards and regenerates any question the vault cannot uniquely answer from its notes
Reads cited staged paths for note claims and marks unsupported claims source: unverified or omits them
Reports how many questions passed, were discarded/regenerated, and claims flagged before proceeding to the quiz
Writes or updates StudyVault/00-Dashboard/Verification Log.md with the audit table
Do not start the quiz until every surviving question passes verification

evals.prompt: Don't mark a concept as mastered after I get one multiple-choice right — I need to actually retain it. Mix sections once I know the basics.
evals.expected_output: Uses a mastery threshold (two corrects including one applied/analysis) before flipping a concept to known, re-tests concepts later in the same session after spacing, and switches to interleaved cross-section questions once basics are green.
expectations: Does not flip a concept to known after a single correct MCQ — requires a mastery threshold (e.g. two corrects including one applied/analysis)
Records partial progress (e.g. in-progress status) until the threshold is met
Re-tests a concept later in the same session after intervening questions; downgrades and re-teaches on failure
Offers interleaved cross-section questions once big-picture basics are past basics or the user opts in
Stays artifact-only — no cross-session spaced-repetition scheduler

evals.prompt: I've read the architecture notes — now make me find things in the actual repo, not just answer multiple choice.
evals.expected_output: Assigns applied/transfer tasks (locate-owner, where-to-add, trace-the-bug, blast-radius) graded against staged repo files once section concepts meet the mastery threshold, with cite-or-refuse answers pointing to real paths under sources/repos/.
expectations: Uses applied/transfer task types for codebase or mixed runs after concepts meet the mastery threshold
Includes locate-owner, where-to-add, trace-the-bug, and blast-radius style prompts
Grades answers against real staged file paths under sources/repos/ (cite-or-refuse)
Teaches from vault notes and staged files on wrong answers instead of scoring a guess
Defines task types and when to assign them in learn-project rather than only in upstream tutor

evals.prompt: The vault is all text — add concept maps and an architecture diagram so I can see how things connect.
evals.expected_output: After tutor-setup, generates Mermaid concept maps per section and an architecture diagram for codebase/mixed runs, embedded in the dashboard MOC and section notes, with nodes/edges grounded in vault wikilinks and staged sources only.
expectations: Generates Mermaid concept maps with one diagram per section (nodes = concept notes, edges from wikilinks or stated prerequisites)
For codebase or mixed runs, generates an architecture diagram from staged repos and architecture notes
Embeds diagrams in StudyVault/00-Dashboard/MOC.md and section index/lead notes
Omits uncited relationships — cite-or-refuse applies to diagram edges as well as prose
Uses fenced mermaid code blocks in the vault markdown files

evals.prompt: I updated the design doc since last time — re-stage and refresh the vault without redoing everything from scratch.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs stage-learn-sources v3 with contentHash comparison: only changed sources re-staged, manifest.freshness reports changed/unchanged keys, and when freshness.changed is non-empty with an existing StudyVault, affected vault sections are treated stale and /tutor-setup re-run for those sections only.
expectations: Reads manifest.json freshness (changed / unchanged keys and per-source contentHash) before deciding what to re-fetch
Re-stages only changed inputs on aggregator re-run — unchanged sources are skipped
When freshness.changed is non-empty and a StudyVault exists, treats notes from those sources as stale
Re-runs /tutor-setup for affected sections only instead of a full regather from Phase 2
Reports which sources changed vs were skipped unchanged in the summary

evals.prompt: Teach me this repo plus the onboarding wiki at https://wiki.example.com/start and the architecture PDF on my desktop — code and docs together.
evals.expected_output: Mixed run: stages local repo + WebFetch web page + loose PDF via --file, manifest tutorSetupMode is mixed, /tutor-setup runs in Document Mode over harvested repo docs plus docs/files/web/context under sources/.
expectations: Stages the local repo with --local and sets mixed mode when repo plus non-code sources are present
WebFetch saves the wiki page to inputs/web/ and passes --web with url:path
Stages the PDF with --file preserving extension for tutor-setup extraction
Runs /tutor-setup in mixed mode (Document Mode over all sources/ material)
Grounds vault notes across repo docs and external doc sources with cite-or-refuse paths

evals.prompt: Start over — wipe ./.learn-project and tutor me fresh on just this repo.
evals.expected_output: When the user explicitly says start over, clears the staging root first, then runs intake → gather → stage → tutor-setup → tutor from scratch on the current repo only.
expectations: Clears or replaces the staging root when the user explicitly requests start over
Does not resume at Phase 6 when start-over was requested even if an old StudyVault existed
Re-runs the full pipeline from intake after clearing — not a partial patch on old vault
Uses the current directory as the local repo source after reset
Tells the user the staging root was cleared and which phase it is starting at

evals.prompt: Tutor me on payments — scan ~/apps and stage every repo you find.
evals.expected_output: Lists ~/apps, shortlists repos whose names match the payments topic, confirms the shortlist with the user before staging many large repos, and only then passes selected paths to --local.
expectations: Lists ~/apps (or the requested parent directory) before staging
Matches repo folder names to the stated topic and builds a shortlist — does not blindly --local every folder
Confirms the shortlist with the user before copying/cloning many large repos
Stages only the confirmed repos with --local
Reports which repos were staged and which were skipped as off-topic

evals.prompt: Give me the learning brief before the quiz — and don't claim anything you can't cite from what you staged.
evals.expected_output: After tutor-setup, presents a concise major-first learning brief drawn from the vault (not a raw dump) with every claim grounded in a staged source path; ends by confirming readiness before /tutor.
expectations: Presents the learning brief after the vault exists and before /tutor starts
Leads with big picture then highest-importance concepts — major-first, not a vault dump
Grounds every factual claim in a staged source path or marks source: unverified
Links each concept to the vault note covering it for deeper reading
Confirms the user has read the brief or asks focus before starting the quiz

evals.prompt: Focus only on authentication and security — skip the billing sections when building the vault.
evals.expected_output: Captures focus areas during intake, weights tutor-setup coverage toward authentication/security, and mastery tracking + question selection prioritize those sections while still cite-or-refuse grounding.
expectations: Records focus areas from intake (authentication and security) with sensible defaults when unspecified
Weights tutor-setup coverage and vault organization toward stated focus areas
Does not skip tutor-setup quality checklist phases (verified source mapping / self-review)
Adaptive drilling prioritizes lowest-known sections within the focus scope
Still grounds all notes and quiz answers in staged material — focus narrows scope, not cite-or-refuse

evals.prompt: The vault practice files are full of 'name the four X' and 'list the three epics' questions — fix them before you quiz me.
evals.expected_output: Audits tutor-setup practice files, rewrites list-recall questions into application/analysis scenarios, caps pure recall at ~30%, shortens concept tracker labels, updates MOC Weak Areas, and adds rendering-modes-vs-delivery-ladder to Exam Traps when architecture is in scope.
expectations: Audits * Practice.md files after tutor-setup and before /tutor
Rewrites pure list/name/ID recall questions into scenario-based application or analysis
Keeps at most ~30% of practice questions as pure recall — prefer meaning over memorization
Uses short canonical labels in concepts/*.md tracker rows (detail lives in linked notes)
Populates or refreshes MOC §Weak Areas from the Learning Dashboard after diagnostic

evals.prompt: Run the quiz-fix loop — Agent B found wrong practice answers, recall over 30%, and ungrounded applied tasks. Fix and re-quiz until clean.
evals.expected_output: Iterates quiz → fix vault/practice → re-run Phase 5c Verification Log → re-quiz with fresh agent personas until zero P0/P1 gaps: wrong answers fixed, recall ≤30% per practice file, applied tasks cite staged repo paths, coarse concepts split, verification log updated.
expectations: Fixes wrong practice-file answers before re-quizzing (cite staged sources)
Brings every * Practice.md recall ratio to at most ~30%
Writes or updates StudyVault/00-Dashboard/Verification Log.md after Phase 5c
Adds grounded vault notes for applied-task prompts (locate-owner, where-to-add) citing sources/repos/
Splits oversized concept tracker rows when mastery % is too coarse (e.g. B5–B11 → B5–B9 + B10–B11)
Re-quizzes with a fresh critical lens after fixes; stops when no P0/P1 gaps remain
